t: Mohists taught impartial care: a person should care equally for all others, whatever their relationship, which set them against the Confucians, who held that love should be unconditional but not indiscriminate.

Mohists formed a disciplined organisation with units in all the major kingdoms and became the pre-eminent siege-defence engineers before the Qin unification, opposing offensive war but accepting force in legitimate defence.

Mohism almost disappeared as an independent school after 221 BCE; the Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy suggests that its more appealing ideas were shared with rival schools by the middle of the former Han dynasty.
dyk: In the story of Gongshu in the Mohist canon, Mozi travelled ten days and nights to Chu, made a wall of his belt and sticks to stand for machines, and showed Gongshu Pan that he could defend Song against any attack; he then announced that three hundred of his disciples were already on Song’s walls, and the king cancelled the invasion.
ev: The Spring and Autumn period begins, the start of the age of the four main philosophic schools that included Mohism
Mozi, the founder of the school, is born
Mozi develops the concept of ai, impartial or universal love, in reaction to Confucianism’s benevolent love
The Qin unification of China ends the wars between states in which Mohist siege-defence skills had been in demand
Jin Guantao, Fan Hongye and Liu Qingfeng argue that Chinese science lacked a definitive structure without a flourishing Mohism

f.thinkers: Mozi (c. 470 BCE – c. 391 BCE), the founder, whose disciples developed the school; the later Mohist logicians, who built on his doctrine; Gongshu Pan, the engineer in the story of the siege of Song, who built machines for the king of Chu; Edward Craig, who prefers the translation “impartial care”; Chris Fraser and Angus C. Graham, modern scholars of the school
f.texts: the Mozi, the book that embodies the school’s doctrine; the Mohist canon (Mo Jing), on logic, mathematics and the physical sciences; the chapters “Against Music” (非樂) of the Mozi
f.ideas: impartial care (兼愛, jiān ài, often translated “universal love”); a consequentialist ethics whose goods are order, material wealth and a growing population; appointment by merit, not by family tie; obedience to Tian, Heaven, and belief in spirits; frugality and austerity, including against lavish funerals and music; opposition to offensive war, with defence permitted; the three criteria (San Biao) for testing views, used against fatalism
f.today: No school or state claims it. Mohism almost disappeared after the Qin dynasty, as it transformed and integrated into sects of Taoism; its logic, science and ethics are studied by modern scholars
